critical.msg: Hardcoded database credentials exposed in docs/EXTERNAL_ACCESS.md - postgresql connection string contains actual hostname and credentials (aws-1-ap-south-1.pooler.supabase.com). This document could be committed to public repos.
SECRET_KEY and JWT_SECRET_KEY exposed in plain text in docs/EXTERNAL_ACCESS.md environment variables section
Framework regression: Migrating from FastAPI to Flask loses async capabilities, automatic OpenAPI docs, and Pydantic validation. FastAPI was async-native with proper dependency injection.
Dependencies not synchronized: Dockerfile hardcodes flask/gunicorn but pyproject.toml has different dependencies. Changes to pyproject.toml won't reflect in container builds.

warnings: Dockerfile removed HEALTHCHECK CMD - reduced container orchestration observability
Removed alembic/ directory copy but alembic.ini remains - potential missing migration files
asyncpg removed from dependencies but still referenced in database connection logic
suggestions: Move credentials to environment variables or secrets manager - never commit to docs
Consider keeping FastAPI for async operations or fully document why Flask is preferred
Add back healthcheck or use orchestrator-level probes (Kubernetes readiness/liveness)
Ensure Dockerfile installs from pyproject.toml to maintain consistency: pip install -e .
llm_parsed.summary: REJECTED - 4 critical issues: (1) SECURITY: Database credentials, SECRET_KEY, JWT_SECRET_KEY hardcoded in docs/EXTERNAL_ACCESS.md - must remove immediately and use env vars.
